papers.title: Bilevel Coordinated Reflection: A Game-Theoretic Approach to Multi-Agent LLM Systems

summary.tldr: A novel game-theoretic framework models multi-agent LLM systems as a bilevel coordination game and introduces Stochastic Reflective Memory Ascent (SRMA), an environment-grounded reflection algorithm with proven exact convergence guarantees.
key_points: Models orchestrator-worker interaction as a bilevel game where workers' local updates form an approximate potential game with equilibrium slack governed by task decomposition quality.

Proves an information-theoretic impossibility result showing transcript-only reflection gates cannot uniformly improve over text-indistinguishable environments, necessitating environment-grounded verification.
Introduces Stochastic Reflective Memory Ascent (SRMA), which accepts candidate memories based on strict evaluation risk reduction and achieves order-tight geometric or polynomial convergence.
Achieves a 72.2% resolution rate on 500 SWE-bench instances using a Kimi-based system implementation compared to 70.8% for the public mini-SWE-agent baseline.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides rigorous theoretical convergence bounds for multi-agent LLM reflection while proving that environment-grounded verification is necessary to prevent persistent performance drift.

papers.title: Iris: Climbing to the Search Frontier

summary.tldr: Iris-mini (35B-A3B) and Iris-pro (397B-A17B) are open-source single-agent search models trained via an iterative SFT-RL climbing recipe using graph-based synthetic task construction.
key_points: Tasks are generated by building multi-hop chains on a web corpus entity graph, obfuscating non-answer entities, and keeping only queries that fail closed-book but pass open-book.
Training uses 'SFT-RL climbing', alternating SFT and live-search RL while returning the hardest, most efficient rollouts back into the next SFT pass.
Inference uses a single ReAct agent without sub-agents or test-time verification, incorporating explicit inference-time context management.
Iris-pro achieves 88.6 on BrowseComp, 85.1 on BrowseComp-ZH, 92.9 on DeepSearchQA, and 56.4 on HLE; Iris-mini achieves 82.2, 84.8, 86.9, and 52.3 respectively.
summary.why_it_matters: The release provides the weights, synthetic data construction pipeline, and training recipe for state-of-the-art open-source web search agents.

papers.title: WorldSculpt: Generating Compositional Worlds from Grounded Videos

summary.tldr: WorldSculpt generates compositional 3D mesh scenes containing hundreds of occluded objects by adapting a single-object 3D generative prior, Pixal3D, with a multi-view conditioning pathway.
key_points: Extends Pixal3D with a multi-view conditioning pathway to ground object generation across multiple posed observations.
Finetuned entirely on single objects in canonical space, achieving generalization to complex, densely cluttered scenes without scene-level training.
Introduces UE-MeshyScene, a photorealistic benchmark featuring hundreds of objects per scene, complete with per-object annotations and ground-truth meshes.
Converts generated 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) worlds, including Marble and HY-World 2.0, into fully compositional mesh scenes.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables the automated creation of fully compositional, editable 3D environments from video inputs for downstream applications in robotics, AR/VR, simulation, and gaming.

papers.title: Enoki: Efficient Multi-Level Hallucination Detection

summary.tldr: Enoki is an Open Information Extraction framework that unifies claim-level verification and span-level localization for LLM hallucination detection without requiring separate alignment steps.
key_points: Uses a shared representation that extracts text-anchored relational facts, verifies them against evidence, and projects unsupported facts back to hallucinated text spans.
Supports LLM-based, encoder-based, and rule-based extraction regimes through a unified interface to balance accuracy and compute overhead.
Outperforms existing methods on fine-grained span- and entity-level localization while using fewer resources than pure LLM-heavy pipelines.
Introduces EnokiQA, a new dual-granularity dataset featuring aligned claim-level verification and span-level localization annotations.
summary.why_it_matters: It significantly reduces the inference cost and pipeline complexity of fine-grained hallucination detection in high-stakes LLM deployments.

papers.title: Ask Before You Optimize: Dynamic Pre-Formulation Clarification for Interactive Optimization

summary.tldr: OR-Clarify introduces a benchmark evaluating LLM optimization agents on pre-formulation clarification, paired with InterOPT, a two-stage framework that identifies missing formulation-critical gaps before generating mathematical programs.
key_points: OR-Clarify evaluates agents using partial public problem descriptions with withheld structured hidden slots via bounded interactions with a simulated user.
The benchmark measures slot recovery, stopping behavior, silent assumptions, and interaction cost across open-ended and choice-based clarification settings.
InterOPT uses a two-stage decision framework to identify unresolved formulation-critical gaps to determine whether to prompt the user or cease interaction.
InterOPT outperformed all baselines in exact slot recovery within choice-based experiments and remained competitive in open-ended settings.
summary.why_it_matters: It shifts operations research LLM evaluation from static text-to-code generation to interactive task completion that handles incomplete, real-world user specifications safely.

papers.title: Don't Drop Dropout: Optimizing Layer Sparsity for Efficient LLM Training and Inference

summary.tldr: A comprehensive study across 2,400+ experiments demonstrates that optimizing layer dropout hyperparameters improves LLM pre-training efficiency and unlocks post-training inference optimizations.
key_points: Optimizing layer dropout distribution, time scheduling, and optimizer hyperparameters reduces training FLOPs by up to 25% for equivalent validation loss.
Enables post-training techniques including early exit, intermediate-layer skipping, and self-speculative decoding, achieving up to 1.5x inference speedup with negligible accuracy loss.
Validated across 2,400+ training runs on Cerebras CS-3 systems, covering models from 271M to 8.2B parameters and datasets up to 160B tokens.
summary.why_it_matters: Reintroducing optimized layer dropout into modern LLM pre-training recipes reduces compute costs for both model training and deployment without sacrificing accuracy.

papers.title: The Attention Triangle in Audio-Video Models

summary.tldr: Researchers analyzed the audio-video-text cross-attention triangle in diffusion models, discovering that parameter-encoded biases along the bidirectional audio-video edge drive semantic leakage, and developed attention-signal interventions to fix cross-modal misalignment.
key_points: Identified the 'attention triangle'—the cross-attention edges connecting text, audio, and video streams—as the primary pathway for semantic routing and leakage.
Found that the audio-video cross-attention edge is bidirectional and heavily influenced by parameter-encoded priors, which can override text prompt conditioning when in conflict.
Extracted attention-derived signals to diagnose internal semantic distribution, deliberately trigger leakage in controlled settings, and isolate specific modal interactions.
Implemented inference-time interventions using attention-derived signals to enforce consistent cross-modal alignment without degrading generation quality.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding and controlling cross-modal attention routing prevents models from ignoring prompt instructions in favor of visually canonical biases during audio-video generation.

papers.title: Beneath the Surface of Chains-of-Thought: A Mechanistic Interpretation of Reasoning Operations in LLMs

summary.tldr: A new mechanistic interpretability study reveals that distinct Chain-of-Thought reasoning operations exhibit separable geometric structures in LLM hidden representations, with separability peaking in middle layers.
key_points: Reasoning operations like problem formulation, goal decomposition, and deduction are geometrically separable in held-out hidden representations, independent of lexical or positional confounds.
Operation separability peaks in the middle layers, with token-wise alignment becoming increasingly distributed over text spans in deeper layers.
Identical surface tokens are embedded differently depending on the reasoning operation of their surrounding chunk.
Attention-masking interventions demonstrate that operation-aligned representations at the start of a chunk rely directly on preceding reasoning context.
summary.why_it_matters: Proving that LLMs maintain geometric representations corresponding to high-level reasoning steps enables better mechanistic understanding, monitoring, and steering of internal Chain-of-Thought processes.

papers.title: RISE: Recursive Improvement via Self-Extrapolating Policy Distillation

summary.tldr: RISE introduces recursive self-distillation by extrapolating parameter or logit displacements along a model's RLVR training trajectory to construct dense, token-level synthetic teacher targets without external models.
key_points: Constructs a synthetic teacher by extrapolating the displacement between the active checkpoint and a trailing anchor in parameter space or output logit space.
Converts sparse, outcome-based RLVR parameter updates into dense, token-level supervision targets without requiring privileged conditioning or external models.
Establishes a recursive improvement loop where outcome rewards ground policy extrapolation and the refreshed teacher refines fine-grained token decisions every iteration.
Outperforms both standalone RLVR and conventional on-policy self-distillation across mathematical reasoning, STEM, code generation, and multi-turn agentic benchmarks.
summary.why_it_matters: It eliminates the performance bottleneck of external or privileged teacher models in on-policy distillation, enabling self-improving post-training via dense token-level feedback.

papers.title: MaxKernel: Agentic Kernel Generation for TPUs

summary.tldr: MaxKernel is an open-source multi-agent system designed for TPU kernel generation, using compiler feedback, specialized sub-agents, and three human or autonomous optimization paradigms.
key_points: Features three kernel development paradigms: Human-in-the-Loop (HITL), Autonomous (Auto) driven by metrics and traces, and Graph-Based Autonomous Search for global design exploration.
Utilizes a shared pool of sub-agents dedicated to planning, implementation, self-debugging, testing, and hardware profiling.
Evaluated on JaxBench, a suite of 50 diverse TPU kernel tasks, as well as complex workloads from state-of-the-art open-source models.
Achieves performance matching expert hand-tuned baselines across benchmark tasks.
summary.why_it_matters: MaxKernel automates the labor-intensive process of writing and optimizing hardware-level TPU kernels, matching human-expert performance without requiring deep hardware specialization.

papers.title: When Models Edit Too Much: On the Fidelity of Minimal Code Edits

summary.tldr: A new framework evaluates LLM code over-editing, showing that preservation instructions and reinforcement learning significantly reduce unnecessary edits while improving Pass@1 performance.
key_points: Over-editing was evaluated using 400 BigCodeBench problems modified with controlled AST-level corruptions to create known minimal patches.
Frontier models like GPT-5.5 frequently rewrite code unnecessarily, showing that high Pass@1 rates can coexist with high added cognitive complexity.
Prompting with a preservation instruction decreased average excess Levenshtein distance from 0.195 to 0.131, cut added cognitive complexity by 26.6%, and increased Pass@1 by 2.3 points.
Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) overfits to known corruption patterns, while reinforcement learning (RL) provides the best out-of-domain edit-fidelity and performance retention.
summary.why_it_matters: Measuring and training for edit fidelity ensures AI-generated code repairs remain minimal, reviewable, and faithful to original developer implementations.

papers.title: τ^τ-Bench: An Environment for End-To-End, Realistic Agent Construction

summary.tldr: τ^τ-Bench evaluates coding agents on building end-to-end customer service agents given raw business records, client requirements, production APIs, cost constraints, and a legacy codebase.
key_points: Evaluates developer agents across 53 tasks in four domains by testing their constructed agents against held-out simulated users.
Top-performing setup (Claude Opus 5 using Claude Code) achieved a pass rate of 23.9% in evaluation simulations.
Human expert-authored reference ceiling achieved an 82.2% pass rate on the same benchmark.
Primary failure modes included shallow record queries, poor client communication, and a lack of architecture and serving-cost optimization.
summary.why_it_matters: The benchmark provides a realistic metric for automated software development by testing whether coding agents can design, optimize, and ship functional production agents under real-world constraints.

papers.title: When Quantization Breaks Memory: Recurrent-State Write-Back in Low-Precision Temporal Inference

summary.tldr: Researchers identify recurrent-state write-back as a primary failure mode in 4-bit RNN inference and propose non-retraining interventions like error feedback to restore state update accuracy.
key_points: Applying deterministic 4-bit state storage post-training to a GRU model increases parameter estimation errors for fluorescence lifetime components tau1 and tau2 by ~70x and ~300x.
Failure occurs because small, repeated state updates fall below the quantization write threshold, causing the stored state to remain static while the network attempts updates.
Error feedback, residual memory, and direction memory recover baseline accuracy without retraining by propagating suppressed sub-threshold update information across time steps.
Post-training tests on an LSTM replicate the failure and show that its cell state is significantly more sensitive to coarse write-back quantization than its hidden state.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that low-precision recurrent inference requires specialized state-storage interfaces or error-feedback mechanisms to prevent compounding memory degradation without expensive model retraining.

papers.title: ShallowStream: Index Shallow then Answer Deep for Streaming Video Understanding

summary.tldr: ShallowStream introduces a framework that uses shallow MLLM layers for low-cost frame encoding and retrieval indexing, executing full-depth processing only during query-time answering.
key_points: Uses shallow-layer KV caches of an MLLM to build and maintain an always-on, lightweight video index during continuous stream processing.
Uses shallow-layer attention scores combined with a diversity-aware selection strategy to identify and retrieve context frames for query answering.
Avoids executing repeated full-depth MLLM prefills on every incoming stream frame, curbing linear KV cache growth relative to model depth.
Reduces per-frame prefill latency by up to 52.1x and 10-second end-to-end latency by up to 11.9x while matching top streaming baseline performance.
summary.why_it_matters: It drastically reduces compute latency and memory overhead for real-time video stream processing in MLLM applications like autonomous driving and robotics.

papers.title: AdaptVPR: Route-Aware Hard Positive Generation for Robust Visual Place Recognition

summary.tldr: AdaptVPR introduces a route-aware generative augmentation framework that synthesizes, verifies, and refines hard positive training images across global appearance, local occlusion, and dual-perturbation routes.
key_points: A vision-language model parses scene attributes to score editability, while a rule-based scheduler selects among Global Appearance, Local Occlusion, and Dual generation routes.
A VPR-oriented verification scheme filters synthetic candidates based on geometric consistency and appearance diversity to prevent structural drift.
Local Occlusion and Dual routes incorporate iterative prompt refinement and regeneration based on verification feedback, whereas Global candidates use a single-pass rejection strategy.
Using the framework, the authors built AdaptCities, a dataset of 160K verified synthetic same-place hard positives.
Evaluation demonstrates top-1 recall (R@1) improvements of up to 9.2% across standard benchmarks and severe domain shifts.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables VPR models to maintain localization accuracy under severe weather, lighting, and occlusion shifts by expanding dataset diversity without structural drift.

papers.title: RISE: Recursive Improvement via Self-Extrapolating Policy Distillation

summary.tldr: RISE recursively improves language models by creating a synthetic teacher that extrapolates trajectory updates between the current RLVR checkpoint and a trailing anchor, providing dense token-level distillation targets without external models.
key_points: Constructs a synthetic teacher by extrapolating parameter-space or logit-space displacement between the active checkpoint and a trailing anchor model.
Converts sparse outcome-based RLVR updates into dense, per-token supervision targets without requiring privileged in-context conditioning.
Establishes a complementary feedback loop where RLVR outcome rewards ground the direction of extrapolation while the extrapolated teacher refines local token decisions.
Refreshes the synthetic teacher at every iteration, converting on-policy distillation from a one-shot compression step into a recursive self-improvement mechanism.
summary.why_it_matters: RISE enables self-contained, iterative post-training optimization that consistently outperforms standard RLVR and on-policy self-distillation across math, code, STEM, and agentic tasks.

papers.title: Don't Drop Dropout: Optimizing Layer Sparsity for Efficient LLM Training and Inference

summary.tldr: A study across 2,400 experiments proves that re-introducing optimized layer dropout into LLM pre-training improves loss and saves up to 25% of training FLOPs.
key_points: Optimizing layer distribution, time schedules, and optimizer hyperparameters allows layer dropout to achieve lower or equal validation loss while saving up to 25% of training FLOPs.
Pre-training with layer dropout enables post-training inference techniques, including early exit, intermediate-layer skipping, and self-speculative decoding, achieving up to 1.5x inference speedup.
Empirical validation spans models from 271M to 8.2B parameters and datasets up to 160B tokens using Cerebras CS-3 systems.
summary.why_it_matters: Properly configured layer dropout lowers the compute required to train state-of-the-art LLMs while unlocking substantial post-training inference acceleration with minimal accuracy loss.

papers.title: ACE: Adaptive Calibration-Free Expert Skipping for MoE-based LLMs

summary.tldr: ACE is a training-free, calibration-free MoE expert skipping framework that dynamically drops low-contribution expert slots at inference using offline-computed spectral and directional metrics.
key_points: Global Spectral Proxy (GSP) estimates overall expert transformation capacity offline using coupled gate, up, and down projections alongside RMSNorm scaling.
Router-Conditioned Refinement (RCR) builds directional prototypes from centered router weights to measure expert response strength along preferred routing vectors.
Dual-view execution always preserves the top-1 expert and only skips a candidate expert slot when both GSP and RCR metrics indicate low contribution.
Online overhead is limited to table lookups and scalar operations, outperforming static and dynamic baselines on downstream tasks.
At a 50% expert skipping ratio on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, ACE lowers WikiText-2 perplexity by 7.96% and raises average accuracy by 4.15 percentage points over top baselines.
summary.why_it_matters: ACE enables significant compute reduction during MoE inference without requiring model retraining, calibration datasets, or modifications to saved model checkpoints.

papers.title: What Matters in On-Policy Distillation? A Perspective on Data Efficiency and Data Selection

summary.tldr: A study on On-Policy Distillation (OPD) reveals that training on as few as 8 selected hard examples matches 17K-example baseline performance, driven by longer Chain-of-Thought (CoT) paths rather than high token entropy.
key_points: Single-example (1-shot) OPD is consistently effective across training samples, with harder problems yielding superior performance gains.

Student model improvements stem from longer CoT paths generated by hard problems—which enable sustained teacher alignment and critical reasoning patterns like reflection—rather than high token entropy.
Unsolvable examples exceeding the teacher model's capabilities can be successfully utilized for training if selected based on difficulty.
Experiments across four 1.5B to 7B parameter models demonstrate that a simple data selection method choosing 8 hard examples achieves parity with a full 17K dataset baseline.
summary.why_it_matters: Demonstrating extreme data efficiency in On-Policy Distillation dramatically reduces the compute and data requirements needed to post-train smaller reasoning models.

papers.title: Unifying ICL, SFT, KL-Regularized RL Through a Bayesian Lens

summary.tldr: A new theoretical note unifies ICL, SFT, KL-regularized RL, and test-time search under a two-step Bayesian framework comprising posterior construction and forward-KL projection.
key_points: Formulates learning methods via a two-step template: constructing a Bayes or Gibbs posterior q* using a reference model and utility signal, then projecting q* onto a parametric family using forward-KL.
Proves that few-shot ICL and SFT operate as in-context and in-weights amortized projections onto the same Bayes posterior predictive distribution.

Shows that KL-regularized RLHF/RLVR, reward-weighted SFT/ICL, and advantage-weighted SFT share equivalent objectives and first-order updates as forward-KL projections onto reward- or advantage-induced posteriors.

Explains modern reasoning paradigms (e.g., DeepSeek-R1, o1) as the combination of test-time Bayesian search with training-time KL amortization, highlighting why cold-start supervised warm-ups are necessary for importance-weighted KL projections.
summary.why_it_matters: Unifying these paradigms provides a theoretical framework to explain empirical anomalies, such as the varied impact of few-shot prompting on RL-tuned reasoning models, and guides the design of modern reasoning pipelines.

papers.title: How to Speculate about Uncertainty in Agentic Coding? A Draft-Model Gate Method

summary.tldr: Speculative Uncertainty (SU) uses a small open-weight draft model in a single forward pass to compute token cross-likelihoods from a black-box LLM agent's output, creating a predictive failure signal without accessing model internals.
key_points: Inverts speculative decoding by evaluating an already-generated trajectory using a draft model to get cross-likelihoods without needing logits, weights, or repeated sampling.
Extracts phase-aware features by analyzing reasoning and action spans separately, calibrating these features against a verifiable objective.
Instantiates a pre-execution veto gate policy evaluated on Qwen3-Coder-480B and Claude 3.5 Sonnet agents.
Reduces execution error rates by 6 to 8 percentage points and cuts deployment token costs by 14% to 19%.
Transfers to out-of-distribution benchmarks without retraining and generalizes across different agent models.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables cost-effective, real-time failure prediction and pre-execution vetoing for black-box AI agents without requiring access to internal model weights or multiple expensive sampling calls.

papers.title: Amortizing Scaling Law Construction Costs

summary.tldr: A novel Bayesian optimization framework constructs accurate foundation model scaling laws while reducing compute costs by 10-100x compared to full grid training.
key_points: Scaling law construction is framed as a Bayesian optimization problem to collect data efficiently instead of training an exhaustive hyperparameter grid.
The framework uses progressive compute budget expansion during acquisition to mimic practical compute-ordered configuration evaluations.
Surrogate-fantasized evaluations augment observed data to reconstruct the full grid and fit scaling laws without running every configuration.
summary.why_it_matters: It dramatically lowers the computational barrier to deriving optimal hyperparameter and parameter scaling laws for foundation models.

papers.title: BeaconKV: Key-Value Cache Compression Guided by Beacon Queries for Efficient Large Reasoning Model Inference

summary.tldr: BeaconKV is a training-free KV cache compression method that uses clustered beacon queries to predict attention to distant context from Thought Revisiting Tokens during long reasoning.
key_points: Identifies that Thought Revisiting Tokens (TRT) break standard KV cache assumptions by re-attending to distant prior context like early task-solving plans.
Observes that TRT queries form a small number of distinct similarity clusters in the embedding space.
Maintains compact representative 'beacon queries' for global query clusters to anticipate future KV pair reuse without storing full query history.
Achieves up to 5.8x KV cache memory reduction and over 4.3x throughput improvement across four open-source LRMs while retaining near-full accuracy.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables deployment of Large Reasoning Models on constrained GPU hardware by substantially reducing memory bottlenecks and boosting throughput during long Chain-of-Thought generation.

papers.title: Cache-Aware Joint Router Adaptation for Memory-Efficient MoE Inference

summary.tldr: A cache-aware post-training framework jointly adapts MoE backbones and auxiliary routers to improve expert-cache hit rates and reduce weight transfers while preserving native Top-K inference.
key_points: Temporal Router updates the model to predict same-layer expert reuse, retaining experts for future tokens without proactive loading.
Spatio-Temporal Router adds a Spatio Router using the causal predecessor's hidden state to pre-fetch and refine the cache before target-layer access.
On Qwen3, Spatio-Temporal Router improves adjusted hit rate by 1.15 to 18.03 points and cuts weight traffic by 4.6% to 53.3% versus the best prefetching baseline.
Ablations show joint post-training of the backbone and auxiliary routers achieves larger cache gains than auxiliary-only tuning while preserving baseline accuracy.
summary.why_it_matters: It reduces memory bandwidth bottlenecks and GPU offloading overhead during MoE decoding without modifying the model's core Top-K inference logic.

papers.title: A Systematic Comparison of Multilingual Interpretability Methods Reveals Anisotropy-Driven Failures

summary.tldr: A systematic evaluation of four multilingual interpretability metrics across 21 models reveals that metric disagreement stems from representation anisotropy, with Inter-Lingual Overlap (ILO) proving to be the only robust predictor of cross-lingual transfer.
key_points: Evaluated four cross-lingual sharing metrics—Centered Kernel Alignment (CKA), ANC, GMM dominance per token, and Inter-Lingual Overlap (ILO)—across 21 base models (125M–14B parameters) from five model families.
Identified anisotropy (representation clustering within a narrow cone of the embedding space) as the cause of performance quantification disagreements among interpretability methods.

Demonstrated that ILO is the only metric whose correlation with downstream cross-lingual transfer across five tasks remains strong (Spearman's ρ = 0.90) after controlling for model size, family, and task variation.
summary.why_it_matters: Researchers evaluating cross-lingual representation sharing should use ILO alongside anisotropy diagnostics instead of metrics like CKA to ensure measurements reliably predict downstream cross-lingual transfer.

summary.tldr: The September 2026 MCP security roundup highlights the Deadbugz supply chain campaign and three new MCP server CVEs.
key_points: The Deadbugz supply chain campaign conceals its payload until the third tool call.
Three new CVEs were identified affecting MCP servers.
summary.why_it_matters: MCP server environments face sophisticated supply chain attacks that evade initial detection alongside newly discovered vulnerabilities.

security.title: When LLM Decompilers Recompile More and Preserve Less

summary.tldr: Researchers introduce Decompile-Diverge, a fuzzing-based behavioral comparison oracle, revealing that LLM decompilers frequently generate recompileable, test-passing code that diverges from original binary behavior or removes security vulnerabilities.
key_points: Evaluated eight LLM decompilation systems across nine configurations using synthesized drivers and reference-grown fuzzing corpora to detect behavioral divergence.
Found that candidates passing all shipped tests still diverge from original binaries on expanded inputs 4.9% of the time overall, and up to 13% for individual systems.
Applying an LLM refinement step to Ghidra output increased the build rate from 75% to 90%, but reduced the behaviorally Matched rate from 74% to 62%.
Up to 10% of tested CVE-grounded functions exhibited Crash Absence, where disclosed vulnerabilities disappeared from the recompiled code without trace.
Source-level analysis revealed divergences are caused by LLMs hallucinating fields, types, callees, and guards instead of leaving explicit placeholders like traditional decompilers.
summary.why_it_matters: Evaluating LLM decompilers solely on recompilability and passing static tests masks semantic errors and security risk alterations, making them unreliable for vulnerability detection and malware analysis.

security.title: Trust-Aware Adaptive Disclosure for Inference Privacy Preservation in Multi-Agent Networks

summary.tldr: A Trust-Aware Privacy Control framework uses dynamic trust relationships and a trust-dependent stochastic policy to adapt message disclosure, reducing adversarial goal inference accuracy in multi-agent consensus networks.
key_points: Addresses privacy-preserving consensus in networked multi-agent systems where agents must hide latent goals from observing adversaries.
Introduces a Trust-Aware Privacy Control framework that dynamically regulates message disclosure based on trust between agents.
Utilizes a trust-dependent stochastic policy to manage information release and balance consensus performance against privacy risks.
Demonstrates reduced adversarial goal inference accuracy compared to baseline methods while preserving network consensus utility.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables critical multi-agent networks, such as healthcare systems and smart grids, to collaborate efficiently without exposing sensitive operational goals to adversarial inference.

security.title: CONTINUITY: Security-Context Contracts for Composable LLM Agent Controls

summary.tldr: CONTINUITY is a framework using assume-guarantee contracts and signed security context to prevent context discontinuity and secure instruction-to-effect paths in composable LLM agent systems.
key_points: Identifies security-context discontinuity, where security controls fail when context is dropped, widened, or rebound across component boundaries.
Carries authenticated context using signed root grants, provenance commitments, transition receipts, bounded releases, transformation witnesses, and effect-bound execution permits.

Formalizes end-to-end consequence integrity to ensure every external effect maps to a valid authorization witness covering principal, task, provenance, delegation, policy, action, and finality boundary.

Tested via a reference verifier and a fault-injection suite covering 32 fault classes across 2,560 parameterized attack instances, resulting in zero harmful external effects while completing 700 benign tasks.
summary.why_it_matters: It proves that individual agent security controls are insufficient unless linked by explicit contracts that prevent authority escalation during component transitions.

security.title: Governing Bring Your Own AI: A Parameterized Maturity Model

summary.tldr: A parameterized governance model introduces a five-level maturity ladder and technical control architecture specifically designed to measure and reduce residual risks associated with unmanaged Bring Your Own AI (BYOAI) tools.
key_points: Defines BYOAI as a distinct form of Shadow AI utilizing employee-authenticated personal accounts operating outside enterprise identity and security controls.
Establishes a governance framework based on a systematic review of 30 records (24 research studies and 6 framework documents), highlighting data exposure and compliance as primary risks.
Structures safeguards around three mutually supporting pillars: technical, governance, and human.
Demonstrates via model results that prohibition-based policies yield residual risk levels similar to unmanaged baselines, whereas layered control architectures significantly reduce exfiltration risk.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that banning personal AI tools is ineffective and provides a quantitative framework for implementing layered technical controls to safely manage unmanaged generative AI usage.

security.title: TIER: Threat Implicitness Benchmark for Evaluating LLM Safety Behaviors

summary.tldr: TIER is a new safety benchmark evaluating LLM behaviors across four risk domains and four threat levels using a six-label behavior scale and two independent LLM judges.
key_points: Evaluates model responses across four threat levels, ranging from explicit harmful requests to sophisticated jailbreak attempts.
Utilizes a six-label behavioral taxonomy evaluated by two independent LLM judges rather than binary pass/fail metrics.
Empirical testing on six open-weight LLMs demonstrates that safety behaviors transition gradually across threat levels rather than shifting abruptly from refusal to compliance.

Reveals that models with identical Attack Success Rates (ASR) display distinct underlying response distributions, with contextual prompts causing the highest behavioral diversity and jailbreaks exposing the largest robustness gaps.
summary.why_it_matters: TIER demonstrates that binary attack metrics miss nuanced behavioral shifts, enabling more granular evaluation of LLM vulnerability across varied threat intensities.

security.title: Forgetting Without Restarting: Execution-State Unlearning for Stateful LLM Agents

summary.tldr: Long-running LLM agents are stateful: beyond the transcript they accrete compressed summaries, plaintext memory, pending tool plans, and, under every serving API, a KV cache. Yet today's "forget" operations delete a plai

security.title: Repeat-After-Me: Black-Box Adaptive Visual Prompt Injection

summary.tldr: Repeat-After-Me is a black-box adaptive visual prompt injection attack that achieves high attack success rates against frontier VLMs where textual prompt injections fail.
key_points: Achieves Attack Success Rates (ASRs) exceeding 80% on open-weight Qwen3.6-27B and 47% on commercial GPT-5.5 under realistic settings without benign prompt authorization.
Demonstrates strong transferability, retaining 43-46% of original ASR across surrogate models and 64-66% across different samples on two commercial victim models.
Enables malicious outputs requiring long or format-compliant strings, such as precise tool calls, PII exfiltration, and Discord-based OpenClaw agent compromise leading to TOOLS.md overwrites.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that visual inputs introduce a severe, transferrable attack vector against commercial VLM agents that bypasses traditional text-based prompt injection defenses.

security.title: Rethinking Indirect Prompt Injection as a Test-Time Search Problem

summary.tldr: A new framework formulates indirect prompt injection as a test-time search problem, utilizing an agentic attacker with a dedicated harness to adaptively discover vulnerabilities based on compute budget.
key_points: Formulates indirect prompt injection as a test-time search over a task-dependent attack surface dictated by the environment, user task, and injection goal.
Implements an agentic attacker that uses environment reconnaissance, structured strategy reasoning, and adaptive feedback from the victim agent.
Demonstrates that scaling attacker test-time compute increases vulnerability discovery and exploitation success.
Shows via ablations that explicit strategy management prevents redundant search paths and maintains performance gains at higher compute budgets.
summary.why_it_matters: Security evaluations for tool-using AI agents must account for the attacker's search methodology and compute budget rather than measuring attack success as a static property of the victim.

security.title: Engineered Persuasion: Evaluating Personalized Pretexts in LLM-Generated Spear Phishing

summary.tldr: A study of 180 working adults evaluated AI-generated phishing emails, finding that each added level of personalization increased convincingness by 2.40 points and click intention odds by 28%, provided details fit the recipient's work context.
key_points: Evaluated four cumulative levels of LLM-generated personalization: workplace (L1), recipient name/title (L2), job responsibilities (L3), and coworker/shared-project context (L4) across 1,436 valid evaluations.
Higher personalization levels increased convincingness by 2.40 points per level (on a 0-100 scale) and increased the odds of expressing click intention by 28% per level.
Messages originating from a named individual referencing a supplied coworker yielded higher convincingness and click intention than messages from a generic department or entity.
Non-clicking participants shifted behavior as personalization increased: reporting declined while deletion increased and investigation remained common.
Qualitative analysis revealed a double-edged effect: role-matched details enhanced credibility, whereas incorrect, vague, or channel-inappropriate details triggered suspicion.
summary.why_it_matters: Cybersecurity training must move beyond teaching employees to spot generic personalized details and focus on evaluating whether pretext context and channels match real-world workplace routines.

security.title: Privacy Failure in Split-LLM Training, The Returned Gradient Nullifies the Decoys

summary.tldr: A two-node split-LLM training system's decoy-based privacy defense fails because zero-value gradients returned from the Trusted Local Node deterministically expose the private, non-decoy rows to the Untrusted Cloud Node.
key_points: In the evaluated split-LLM system, decoy activations are added to forward frames but ignored by the loss, causing their returned gradients to be exactly zero.
Across nine seeds, gradient zero-patterns identified 100% of real activation rows (4,096 of 4,096 per run) while passing initial forward-channel privacy and model quality checks.
An attack on frame contents recovered +0.65 to +1.50 percentage points more tokens over baseline, while shuffled-label controls recovered zero.
Clipping and adding noise to individual gradient rows mitigated the leak at a loss of ~0.01 nats of held-out cross-entropy, though multi-step accumulation attacks remain unmeasured.
summary.why_it_matters: Evaluating privacy solely on the forward activation channel creates a false sense of security, as backward gradient returns can completely compromise decoy-based obfuscation schemes.

security.title: Machine Unlearning as Private Retroactive Algorithms

summary.tldr: A new framework for private retroactive algorithms combines differential privacy under continual observation with retroactivity requirements to provide formal privacy semantics for machine unlearning.
key_points: Reinterprets machine unlearning as data maintenance (retroactive algorithms) rather than pure privacy, due to the lack of meaningful privacy semantics against adversaries observing sequential releases.
Formulates a definition of private retroactive algorithms integrating retroactivity with differential privacy under continual observation.
Provides algorithmic constructions for linear statistics, clustering, and histograms that achieve retroactivity at no asymptotic privacy cost over differential privacy alone.
Establishes theoretical impossibility results outlining the limitations of private retroactive algorithms.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes a rigorous mathematical foundation for machine unlearning by guaranteeing that updated model outputs reflect modified data histories without increasing asymptotic privacy costs.

summary.tldr: This paper explores the application of Conformal Prediction (CP) to offensive security, focusing on Privacy-Preserving Machine Learning and network traffic analysis.
key_points: Identifies a research gap in using Conformal Prediction (CP) for offensive security capabilities despite its popularity in defensive measures.
Presents initial findings applying CP to Privacy-Preserving Machine Learning attacks.
Demonstrates the use of CP techniques in offensive network traffic analysis.
summary.why_it_matters: It expands the understanding of Conformal Prediction by demonstrating how an uncertainty quantification tool can be used to execute cyber attacks rather than just defend against them.

security.title: Federated Attack Campaign Detection via Contrastive Encoding of Threat Indicators in Gradient Updates

summary.tldr: FedIoC is a modular federated learning framework that embeds structured threat indicators into local gradient updates using supervised contrastive loss, enabling servers to cluster cross-organizational attack campaigns via gradient geometry.
key_points: Uses a client-side supervised contrastive loss on IoC-matched network flows to group campaign-relevant embeddings within training batches.
Expresses campaign structure directly in the gradient direction, producing aligned updates across clients observing fragments of the same campaign.
Clusters client updates at the server using cosine similarity to discover global attack patterns without transmitting raw IoC data.
Evaluated on two public threat-detection benchmarks with FL clients holding non-IID data fragments and disjoint indicator sets.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables multi-organization cyberattack campaign detection and threat intelligence sharing while preserving privacy and complying with data-sharing restrictions.

security.title: Why Is SHAP Not a Reliable Standalone Explanation Framework for Malware Detection?

summary.tldr: A theoretical and empirical evaluation demonstrates that SHAP is unreliable as a standalone explanation framework for malware detection due to feature dependencies and off-manifold coalition queries.
key_points: SHAP explains a user-defined feature-coalition game dictated by choices in background distribution, missing feature rules, and input mappings rather than actual malware behavior.

Theoretical proofs show conditional SHAP dilutes feature credit by a factor of 1/m across m-1 redundant features, assigns importance to unused features, and can reverse an unused feature's attribution sign under distribution shifts.
Interventional SHAP evaluates off-manifold feature coalitions that produce synthetically invalid executables not found in real-world data.
Experiments validating these structural failure modes were conducted on EMBER-2018, EMBER-2024, and BODMAS benchmarks using fixed LightGBM and XGBoost models.
summary.why_it_matters: Security analysts cannot rely on SHAP alone to verify if a machine learning detector has learned true malicious functionality versus dataset artifacts without explicit domain validation.

infra.title: Serving LLMs on Tenstorrent Hardware: Inside the vLLM TT Plugin

summary.tldr: Tenstorrent accelerators are now integrated into vLLM via an out-of-tree platform plugin that uses hand-written TTNN implementations from TT-Metal.
key_points: Registers models via a TT-prefixed architecture convention (e.g., TTQwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration) that resolves directly to implementations in TT-Metal.
Supports custom model loading without source edits using the EXTRA_MODELS_DIR environment variable and a vllm_metadata.json configuration.
Supports multimodal and text models out-of-the-box, including Llama 3.2 Vision, Qwen-VL, Qwen 3.6, Mistral 3, and Gemma 3.
Targets hardware setups ranging from small on-card core meshes (n150, n300) up to 32-chip Wormhole Galaxy systems using FABRIC_1D, FABRIC_2D, and FABRIC_1D_RING mesh topologies.
summary.why_it_matters: Users can serve LLMs on Tenstorrent mesh architectures using standard OpenAI-compatible vLLM APIs without modifying core vLLM code.

summary.tldr: OpenAI's Jakub Pachocki reflects on the alignment challenges posed by increasingly capable AI, advocating for enhanced safeguards and global coordination.
key_points: Jakub Pachocki highlights the growing difficulty of aligning increasingly capable AI systems.
The reflection emphasizes the need for stronger technical and operational safeguards.
International coordination is highlighted as a critical component for managing advanced AI risks.
summary.why_it_matters: As AI capabilities advance, maintaining alignment requires coordinated global action and robust safety protocols to prevent potential risks.

vendors.title: Research acceleration: The view inside OpenAI

summary.tldr: OpenAI has shared early internal data on how coding agents are accelerating AI research through increased experiment velocity and handling of complex tasks.
key_points: Internal usage of autonomous coding agents is transforming OpenAI's AI research workflows.
Early data focuses on metrics including agent adoption, experiment velocity, and task complexity.
summary.why_it_matters: Demonstrates the practical impact of using autonomous coding agents to accelerate technical AI research and development inside a leading lab.

vendors.title: Research acceleration: The view inside OpenAI

summary.tldr: OpenAI published details on how its internal research team uses coding agents and Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI) to accelerate AI development.
key_points: OpenAI internal essays highlight Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI) as a central focus for reaching AGI.
Agentic engineering adoption accelerated significantly among OpenAI researchers throughout 2026.
A sharp increase in AI compute spend per researcher in late July suggests internal testing of the model later released as GPT-6 Astra.
summary.why_it_matters: Internal usage patterns at OpenAI indicate that AI-driven coding agents are actively automating and scaling the research required to build next-generation models.

key_points: Partnership formed between OpenAI, AIRPPU, and WAN-IFRA.
